question: Credit of invention of the Chess game goes to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The game of chess is believed to have originated in India during the Gupta Empire in the 6th century AD.
 
• It was initially called "Chaturanga," which means "four divisions of the military" - infantry, cavalry, elephants, and chariots, which are represented by the pieces that would evolve into the modern pawn, knight, bishop, and rook, respectively.
 
• The game spread from India to Persia, where it became known as "Shatranj."
 
• From Persia, the game spread to the Islamic world and then to Europe, where it evolved into the modern game of chess we know today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chaturanga:**

 
 
• Chaturanga is an ancient Indian strategy game that is considered the ancestor of chess.
 
• The game simulates a battle, with each type of piece representing different military units.
 
• The objective of the game was similar to that of chess - to checkmate the opponent's king.
 
 
 
• **Shatranj:**
 
 
• Shatranj is the Persian adaptation of Chaturanga, which was played in the medieval Islamic world.
 
• Shatranj introduced several changes to the original game, including new rules and the renaming of pieces.
 
• The game of Shatranj is very similar to modern chess, with some differences in the movement of pieces.
 
 
 
• **Evolution to Modern Chess:**
 
 
• As the game spread to Europe, it underwent several transformations.
 
• The modern rules of chess began to take shape in Spain and Italy during the 15th century.
 
• The game continued to evolve, with the introduction of the queen's powerful movement and the standardization of the rules in the 19th century.
 
 
 
• **Chess in the Modern World:**
 
 
• Today, chess is a global game played by millions of people worldwide.
 
• It is recognized as a sport and has a well-organized system of tournaments and championships.
 
• The game is also used as a tool for educational purposes, promoting critical thinking, strategy, and cognitive skills.
